'''Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine'''（伊豫豆比古命神社）is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Iaisou Town, {{ill|Matsuyama|an|Matsuyama|ar|ماتسوياما (إهيمه)|arz|ماتسوياما|az|Matsuyama|azb|ماتسویاما، اهیمه|ban|Matsuyama, Éhimé|be|Мацуяма|bg|Мацуяма|ca|Matsuyama|ce|Мацуяма|ceb|Matsuyama (kapital sa prepektura)|cs|Macujama|da|Matsuyama|de|Matsuyama|el|Ματσουγιάμα|eo|Macujama|es|Matsuyama|et|Matsuyama|eu|Matsuyama|fa|ماتسویاما، اهیمه|fi|Matsuyama|fr|Matsuyama (Ehime)|ga|Matsuyama|gl|Matsuyama|hak|Matsuyama-sṳ|he|מצויאמה|hu|Macujama|hy|Մացույամա|id|Matsuyama, Ehime|ilo|Matsuyama|is|Matsuyama|it|Matsuyama|ja|松山市|ko|마쓰야마시|lt|Macujama|lv|Macujama|mdf|Мацуяма|mg|Matsuyama|mi|Matsuyama|mr|मात्सुयामा|mzn|ماتسویاما، اهیمه|nl|Matsuyama|no|Matsuyama (Ehime)|os|Мацуямæ|pl|Matsuyama|pt|Matsuyama (Ehime)|ro|Matsuyama|ru|Мацуяма|sc|Matsuyama|sco|Matsuyama|sh|Matsujama|simple|Matsuyama|sr|Мацујама|su|Matsuyama, Ehime|sv|Matsuyama|sw|Matsuyama, Ehime|szl|Matsuyama|tg|Матсуяма|th|มัตสึยามะ|tl|Matsuyama|tr|Matsuyama|tt|Мацуяма|tum|Matsuyama|uk|Мацуяма|ur|ماتسویاما، اہیمے|uz|Matsuyama|vec|Matsuyama|vi|Matsuyama|war|Matsuyama, Ehime|wuu|松山市|zh|松山市|zh_classical|松山市|zh_min_nan|Matuyama-chhī|zh_yue|松山|qid=Q200022|lt=Matsuyama}}, {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|en|Ehime Prefecture|qid=Q123376|lt=Ehime Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} and an old {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度}}. The shrine crest is a sixteen-petaled chrysanthemum. Locally, it is also known as '''Tsubaki Shrine''' or '''O-Tsubaki-san'''.

The shrine is sometimes spelled with づ tsu and sometimes with a ず. The kana are pronounced identically in most dialects of Japanese though. The shrine officially uses づ,

== deity ==
* {{ill|Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto|qid=Q135505756}} (male deity)
* {{ill|Iyozuhime-no-Mikoto|qid=Q135505758}} (female deity)
* {{ill|Iyonushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q135505760}} (male deity)
* {{ill|Ehime-no-Mikoto|ja|愛比売命}} (female deity)

According to the "{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}" and "{{ill|Kujiki|lt=Kujiki|lt=Kuni no miyatsuko hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuni no miyatsuko hongi}}," Iyonushi-no-Mikoto is the first generation of the {{ill|Kume clan|ja|久味国造|qid=Q21652982|lt=Kumi no Kuni no miyatsuko}}. There are theories that Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto and Iyonushi-no-Mikoto are the same or that Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto is the ancestor deity and Iyonushi-no-Mikoto is his successor.

Additionally, the name of Ehime Prefecture comes from Ehime-no-Mikoto, and Ehime is the only prefecture in Japan named after a deity.

== History ==
In ancient times, the area around the shrine was a sea, and it was called "Tsu-waki Shrine" (Tsu meaning "sea"). Over time, this changed to "Tsubaki Shrine." Additionally, various types of camellia (椿) trees, including Japanese camellia, grow naturally around the shrine, which contributed to its current name.

According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōrei|en|Emperor Kōrei|qid=Q313041|lt=Emperor Kōrei}}. The 2250th anniversary of its founding was celebrated in 1962 (Showa 37), and the 2300th anniversary in 2012 (Heisei 24).

It is identified as the Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine listed in the "{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳}}" (a small shrine). However, it is also speculated to be the major shrine of Iyo, but the leading contender for that designation is {{ill|Iyo Shrine|ja|伊予神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iyo Shrine}} in {{ill|松前町|ja|松前町|zh|松前町|zh_yue|松前町|qid=Q1307271}}, Iyo District.

In the Edo period, it received fervent devotion from the {{ill|Hisamatsu clan|de|Matsudaira (Hisamatsu)|ja|久松氏|qid=Q11369441}}, the lords of the {{ill|Iyo-Matsuyama Domain|fa|قلمرو ایو–ماتسویاما|fr|Domaine de Matsuyama|ja|伊予松山藩|ko|이요 마쓰야마번|pt|Domínio de Iyo-Matsuyama|ru|Иё-Мацуяма (княжество)|zh|松山藩 (伊予國)|qid=Q1042087|lt=Matsuyama Domain}}. Today, the shrine is widely respected for bringing good luck and prosperity, with worshippers from all over the country.

== Outer and Inner Grounds ==
* Shrine name Board: A large stone monument at the Tsubaki Shrine Entrance Intersection, where National Route 33 and Prefectural Route 19 intersect.
* East Grand Torii Gate: A giant red torii gate spanning Prefectural Route 19 on the east side.
* West Grand Torii Gate: A giant red torii gate spanning Prefectural Route 19 on the west side.
* Grand Torii: The torii gate at the entrance to the shrine grounds.
* Main Gate (Zuishinmon): Statues of the right and left ministers.
* Main Shrine: Haiden, Honden, and corridors.
* Tsubaki Prayer Hall: Built in Heisei 12 (2000) on the site of the former Dance Hall (1837-2000). It serves as the shrine office and waiting room.
* Sub-Shrine, Soja Shrine: Dedicated to {{ill|Shionaru Takutsuna no Okina no Kami|ja|潮鳴栲綱翁神}}. According to legend, when Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto and Iyozuhime-no-Mikoto docked their ship at Mount Funayama, this deity welcomed them. Therefore, it is customary to first visit Soja Shrine when worshipping at Iyozuhiko-no-Mikoto Shrine.
* Sub-Shrine, Katsuyuki Hachiman Shrine: Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|qid=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ōjin}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) and {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}. It was established to commemorate the military victories of the {{ill|Kōno clan|ja|河野氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kono clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11554232}} during the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|qid=Q208156|lt=Mongol Invasions of Japan}}. Known as "Shogun-san," it is revered for success in battles, exams, and academics.
* Sub-Shrine, Mikura Shrine: Dedicated to {{ill|Ukanomitama|ja|宇迦之御霊神}}. It is the local deity of the Iaisou district, protecting the prosperity of businesses and family fortunes.
* Sub-Shrine, Komori Shrine: Dedicated to {{ill|Mikumari|ja|水分神|fr|Mikumari|sv|Mikumari|ja|天水分神|lt=Ame-no-Mikumari-no-Kami}} (Heavenly Water Distribution deity) and {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|az|Konohanasakuya|ca|Konohana no Sakuya hime|de|Konohanasakuyahime|fa|کونوهاناساکویا-هیمه|fr|Konohana-no-Sakuya|it|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|コノハナノサクヤビメ|ko|고노하나노사쿠야비메|mni|ꯀꯣꯅꯣꯍꯅꯁꯀꯨꯌ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Konohanasakuya-hime|ru|Коноханасакуя-химэ|sv|Konohanasakuyahime|th|เซ็นเง็ง|vi|Konohana Sakuya Hime|zh|木花開耶姬|qid=Q1781862}}. These deities are revered for child-rearing and safe childbirth. After a child's [[Miyamairi|first shrine visit]], parents pray for their child's growth and offer {{ill|Bib|en|bib|qid=Q407378|lt=bibs}}.

== Tsubaki festival ==
Held on the old calendar January 7-9.

In the past, the festival was held only on the old calendar January 8 and was called "O-Yōka" (おようか). Today, it is held over three days (January 7-9). It is also known as "O-Tsubaki-san" and "The festival that Calls Spring to Iyo." During the festival, tens of thousands of people visit, making it the largest festival in Shikoku in terms of the number of visitors.

The ceremonies during the festival include the opening of the gates at midnight on the 7th, the Spring Grand festival at 9 AM on the 8th, the rear shrine festival at 6 PM on the 9th, and the closing of the gates at midnight. Additionally, special ceremonies such as the Lending Money ceremony, the Secret Procession, and the Combined Fire are held.

The Lending Money ceremony involves borrowing a sacred coin (20 yen) from the shrine and returning double the amount the following year, symbolizing a promise to work diligently and repay more.

The Secret Procession occurs on the night of the 8th, where the shrine's portable shrine is carried to the {{ill|Kotohira shrines|ja|金刀比羅神社|lt=Konpira Shrine}} in Kitadoi Town. The procession is carried out quietly until the portable shrine passes through the main gate, hence the name "Secret Procession."

The Combined Fire, also known as the Five Feast Fires, involves residents along the procession route burning their New Year's decorations to welcome the portable shrine.

== Notes ==
* In 2013, to commemorate the 2300th anniversary of the shrine's establishment, paintings and sliding door paintings by artist {{ill|Taisuke Hamada|ja|浜田泰介|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisuke Hamada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11557983}} and sculptures by sculptor {{ill|Nobuyuki Ishimizu|ja|石水信至}} were dedicated to the shrine.
* The honorary chief priest, Nobuaki Chōsokabe, served as the chairman of the {{ill|Shinto Association of Spiritual Leadership|ja|神道政治連盟|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto Seiji Renmei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590929}} and as a representative of the {{ill|Nippon Kaigi|en|Nippon Kaigi|qid=Q11507216|lt=Nippon Kaigi}} until 2016.
